 Full timeline of investigation into Malayshia Alford's murder 
 Malayshia Alford, 10, was found dead in the trunk of a car in Lindenwold, New Jersey, after going missing in West Philadelphia more than a week earlier. 
 By Brendan Brightman • 
 Published November 5, 2026 • 
 Updated on November 6, 2026 at 1:00 pm 
 BOOKMARKER 
 NBC Universal, Inc. 
 A foster mom was charged with the murder of a child in her care on Thursday. NBC10’s Shaira Arias and Matt DeLucia has the story. 
 Thursday's press conference where murder and related charges were brought against the foster mom of 10-year-old Malayshia Alford was the culmination of several weeks of investigation. 
 The saga began on Oct. 22, when Alford was last seen alive at the home of the foster mom, Carprice Williams, 36, along the 500 block of North Simpson Street in West Philadelphia.

   WATCH HERE 
 She was then reported missing to the Philadelphia Police Department on Oct. 26. That same day, at around 2 a.m., surveillance video captured someone removing what investigators believe was Alford's body from Williams' home. 
 View this post on Instagram 
 On Monday, Nov. 2, police searched around Alford's neighborhood using cadaver dogs. The Pennsylvania State Police also put out a missing persons flyer saying that they believe Alford may be at risk for harm or injury. 
 On Wednesday, Nov. 4, investigators were able to track down a car in Lindenwold, New Jersey, at around 11 p.m., where Alford's body was found. 
 The surveillance video from Oct. 26 was able to be used to track down a suspect car involved in the moving of Alford's body, which then led to the locating of an unidentified person who then helped investigators locate Alford's body, according to Assistant District Attorney Ashley Toczylowski.

 On Thursday, Nov. 4, charges were announced against Williams at a press conference including Philadelphia District Attorney Larry Krasner and Philadelphia Police Commissioner Kevin Bethel. 
 Williams was charged with murder, endangering the welfare of a child, criminal use of a communication facility, possession of an instrument of crime, reckless endangerment, tampering with evidence and abuse of corpse.
